title: Correct pulling force F
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (1) must be 18 N.

title: Correct friction coefficient
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (2) must be √3/15 or its decimal equivalent (~0.1155).

title: Correct horizontal force F0
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (3) must be approximately 9.9 N (or 2.2 N if considering downward acceleration).

title: Accelerations from graph
description: Important: The student must correctly extract the accelerations (a1 = 12 m/s², a2 = -6 m/s²) from the velocity-time graph.

title: Newton's law for first phase
description: Important: The student must apply Newton's second law correctly for the first phase: F - mg sinθ - μ mg cosθ = m a1.

title: Newton's law for second phase
description: Important: The student must apply Newton's second law correctly for the second phase: -mg sinθ - μ mg cosθ = m a2.

title: Horizontal force components
description: Important: For part (3), the student must correctly resolve the horizontal force F0 into components parallel and perpendicular to the incline.

title: Sign error in accelerations
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student uses incorrect signs for the accelerations (e.g., treating a2 as positive).

title: Friction direction error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student misidentifies the direction of the friction force in any of the three scenarios.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Award if the student explicitly shows unit analysis or maintains consistent units throughout.
